terms.meaning: A tool that transforms CSS style files using a list of plugins.
A plugin that adds browser-specific prefixes to style rules so older browsers still work.
A styling system where small class names like text-white apply single style rules directly in the page markup.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Styling tools hooked into the build
sections.what: Lists two styling tools, Tailwind and Autoprefixer, so that the build runs them on the site's style code. Visitors see the finished styles, not this file.
sections.why: Likely reason: Tailwind and Autoprefixer only work when PostCSS runs them.
sections.watch_out: Both plugins must stay installed; removing one silently breaks the matching styles.

summary: A small settings file that tells the build step to run Tailwind and Autoprefixer on the style sheets.
purpose: Connects the styling tools to the build so that Tailwind class names become real CSS and browser prefixes are added automatically.
why: Likely reason: Tailwind needs PostCSS to turn its class names into styles. Reason not stated in the code.
how: During a build or development run, PostCSS reads this file, runs the Tailwind step first, then the Autoprefixer step, and passes the result to the browser.
inputs: Style files, mainly app/globals.css, and the Tailwind configuration.
outputs: Finished CSS that the browser can use.
risks: If a plugin is removed, Tailwind class names such as those in the pages will stop producing styles.
debug: If styles are missing everywhere, confirm this file is present and the plugin names match installed packages.
